# Genesis Apocryphon Column 19 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 19 | **Condition:** Well preserved; major sections legible

---

**19:1** Then I, Abram, traveled across the land from one end to the other, surveying it as I went.

**19:2** I journeyed from the Gihon River to the seacoast, following along the Mediterranean

**19:3** until I reached the Taurus Mountains. Then I traveled from the shore of this great salt sea

**19:4** and went along the Taurus range eastward across the breadth of the land

**19:5** until I came to the Euphrates River. I followed the Euphrates until I reached the Red Sea in the east.

**19:6** I continued along the Red Sea until I came to the Gulf of the Sea of Reeds.

**19:7** Then God said to me: All of this land I will give to you, and to your descendants after you;

**19:8** they will possess it forever. I will multiply your descendants until they are like the dust of the earth —

**19:9** so many that no one can count them. Just so, your descendants will be beyond all counting.

**19:10** Get up and walk through it, from end to end, and see it all, for I am giving it to you.

**19:11** So I, Abram, went and settled near the great oaks of Mamre at Hebron.

**19:12** There I built an altar and made a burnt offering and a grain offering upon it

**19:13** to God Most High. I ate and drank there, together with all the men of my household.

**19:14** I sent word and invited Mamre, Ornam, and Eshkol — the three Amorite brothers who were my allies — and they shared the meal with me.

**19:15** Before those days, a famine had struck the whole land. So I, Abram, went down to Egypt

**19:16** and entered the country. I lived in the land of Egypt for five years before my wife was taken from me.

**19:17** Now the king of Zoan provided us with plenty of grain, oil, and wine,

**19:18** and one night I had a dream. In my dream I saw a cedar tree and a palm tree sprouting from the same root.

**19:19** Men came, meaning to chop down the cedar and leave the palm standing alone.

**19:20** But the palm cried out: Do not cut down the cedar! We both spring from the same root!

**19:21** And so the cedar was saved because of the palm.

**19:22** I woke from my sleep that night and said to my wife Sarai:

**19:23** I have had a dream, and it frightens me. She replied: Tell me about it.

**19:24** So I told her everything, and she grasped its meaning at once. She said to me:

**19:25** They will try to kill you but spare me. Here is the one kindness you must show me:

**19:26** wherever we go, tell people about me: She is my sister. That way I will survive because of you,

**19:27** and my life will be spared on your account.

**19:28** That night Abram wept bitterly over his wife Sarai.

**19:29** I prayed through the night, pleading and begging, and in my anguish I cried out:

**19:30** Blessed are You, O God Most High, my Lord, sovereign over all the ages!

**19:31** You are Lord and Master of all. You rule over every king on earth

**19:32** and bring judgment on them all. Now I bring my case before You

**19:33** against Pharaoh Zoan, king of Egypt, because my wife has been seized from me by force.

**19:34** Pass judgment on him for my sake! Raise Your mighty hand against him and against his entire household!

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 19 is well preserved and opens the Abrahamic narrative. The cedar-and-palm dream is a stunning literary creation unique to this scroll — a parable within a narrative. "Mediterranean" and "Taurus Mountains" are used for clarity. The dream interpretation in 19:25 has Sarai understanding that Abram (the cedar) will be targeted while she (the palm) will be spared. The prayer (19:29-34) anticipates the plagues narrative in Column 21. Dynamic renderings aim to preserve the emotional urgency of the first-person account.*
